For our Jesus knows that there are ears besides these fleshly ones, of which he says: "He that hath ears to hear, let him hear." In these ears, then, Jesus reads the law. If then we understand the women and infants and proselytes separately, and perceive them to be as it were a certain following of the Church, as "in a great house there are also vessels of wood and of earth", we say indeed that strong meat is given to the strong men, of whom it is said: "But strong meat is for the perfect", of whom the church is prepared which "hath not spot or wrinkle". But those whom he calls women, infants and proselytes we understand to be those who still "have need of milk", or who, being also weak like women, "eat herbs". But if one takes the whole church together, the men are understood as those who stand perfect in all things, "armed against the deceits of the devil"; the women, those who do not yet of themselves do what is profitable but by following the examples of the better, who are their head; "for the head of the woman is the man". The infants will be those who, having lately received the faith, are nourished with the milk of the Gospel; and the proselytes, the catechumens, or those who already strive to be joined to the faithful.
08_interl125: the lowest; he that is weak, let him eat herbs
08_interl126: the catechumens, who have need of milk
08_marg76: ADAMANTIUS. From the things that were done let us contemplate the wars and triumphs of the Lord Jesus; although we see these too visibly fulfilled in him. For the kings of the earth, the senate, the people and the Roman princes came together to fight against the name of Jesus and Israel at once. For they decreed by their laws that there should be no Christians. Every city, every order assails the Christian name. But as then all those kings, coming together, could do nothing against Jesus, so now too neither these princes nor the opposing powers have been able to prevent the race of Christians from spreading more widely and deeply. For it is written: "The more they oppressed them, the more they multiplied." And we trust that not only have the invisible enemies been unable to overcome us, but that swiftly, our Lord Jesus conquering, Satan will be crushed under the feet of his servants.
08_marg77: ADAMANTIUS. "In my Father's house there are many mansions." Many too are the differences of those who are in salvation or come to it. Whence I think the Gabaonites are a certain small portion of those who are to be saved, but not without the mark of some infamy. For they become hewers of wood and carriers of water for the service of the people and the altar, because they came with guile to the children of Israel, clothed in old rags and shoes, bringing food of stale bread. These, then, come to Jesus with their oldness, yet asking to be saved. For there are in the Church those who believe indeed and assent to the divine precepts, who are devout and dutiful toward the servants of God and ready enough for the adornment or ministry of the Church, but in their own conversation foul and wrapped in vices, and, by no means "putting off the old man with his deeds", apply no amendment or renewal of morals. To these, then, Christ Jesus grants salvation, but they do not escape a certain mark of infamy. Similar is what is said of such in the book of the Shepherd: that there is a certain tree called the elm, which bears no fruit, yet carries the fruitful vine; and so it is necessary, because it serves the fruit-bearing vine. So the Gabaonites have not put off the old man with his deeds, but they minister to the saints and serve and render some usefulness, and so they receive salvation from Jesus with the interposition of an oath. And note that the heretics who do not receive the Old Testament say at this place: "See that Jesus son of Nave had nothing of humanity, that, granting salvation to men who had come to him as suppliants, he inflicted on them the mark of infamy and the yoke of servitude." But Jesus judged fittingly according to the measure of their faith. For Rahab the harlot, who believed with whole faith with all her house and received the spies with full devotion, was received wholly into the fellowship of the people and "added to the children of Israel". But these, who loved not so much the fellowship of the Israelite people as, from fear of their own destruction, came deceitfully to Jesus, how could they by servile guile merit freedom of life and fellowship in the kingdom? Therefore, though they said, "We have heard how great things the Lord did for you through the Red Sea and in the desert", they yet did nothing worthy of so great a faith. Jesus therefore, seeing their purpose narrow in faith, keeps toward them a most just moderation, so that they who have little faith merit salvation, yet do not receive the height of the kingdom or of freedom, because their faith is ennobled by no addition of works. "But faith without works is dead." But we must take care, while we have power, that, casting away the old filth and the old rags of vices, we be joined to Israelite freedom. For it is commanded in the law that a Hebrew boy, if he should fall into servitude, may not serve more than six years, but in the seventh is to be let go free; so great was the care of freedom among the Israelites. Thou then, if thou art a Hebrew boy and hast fallen into servitude (for he is a boy who through easiness of mind falls into servitude; "but whosoever committeth sin is the servant of sin"; into this servitude a manly and perfect mind does not fall, but a boyish and easy one), thou then, if thou art a Hebrew boy, that is, one of the faithful already baptized, and hast afterwards lapsed into sin, let it suffice thee to have served six years. In the seventh see that thou serve not, but return to thy freedom. Seven signifies the law of the commandments, six the world. While, then, thou savourest "the things that are of the world" and art occupied with them and "thinkest according to the flesh", thou must needs serve sin. When then thou comest to seven, that is, to the knowledge of the law, then seek thy freedom; lest, if thou persevere in sins, with the mark fixed in thy ear, because thou hearest not the words of God moving thee and calling thee back to thy former freedom, thou become the servant of sin for ever.
08_interl127: desiring to become allies of the Israelites not sincerely nor wholly
08_interl128: namely, the old filth and the old rags of the vices
08_interl129: namely, "the old man with his deeds"
08_interl131: "I am with you even to the consummation of the world."
08_interl132: among the saints, who are always ready to fight against the powers of the air
08_interl133: namely, in revelation, of which it is said: "Open my eyes", etc.
08_interl135: they confess that they have heard and know the divine wonders, yet they do nothing worthy of wonder at such great powers
08_marg78: AUGUSTINE. It is asked how the Hebrews believed the oath was to be kept to the Gabaonites, to whom they had sworn as to men coming from a far land, as those had lied. For they knew they would be overthrown in war if it were known to the Hebrews that they dwelt in that land which they were to receive. To them, then, lying that they had come from a far land, they swore; but after they learned that they dwelt where they were to overthrow all whom they found according to God's command, they yet would not break the oath; and although they had learned that those had lied, they chose to spare them, when they could have said that they had sworn as to those whom they believed them to be, that is, men coming from afar, and that when they learned otherwise the command of the Lord concerning them had to be fulfilled, that they should be overthrown like the rest. But God approved this, nor was he angry with those who spared them, although they had not asked him who those men were, and though they had chosen to deceive. Whence they are to be believed, even if they wished to deceive for their own safety, yet to have feared God in his people without deceit. Therefore the Lord was not angry with those who swore or those who spared, and afterwards avenged these same Gabaonites, as men of his own people, on the house of Saul, as the history of the Kings shows. And because the oath was kept thus, though to lying men, so that the sentence was bent toward clemency, it did not displease God. For if, on the contrary, they had sworn to kill some whom they thought to be Gabaonites dwelling in the land, and had afterwards learned that they were foreign to that land and had come to them from afar, it is not to be thought that they would not have spared them, for the sake of fulfilling the oath; since for the sake of that very clemency of sparing, holy David, after he had sworn to kill Nabal, knowing indeed whom he was going to kill, chose to spare him and not fulfil the oath by the harsher law, judging it more pleasing to God if he did not do what he had sworn when disturbed by anger than if he had done it.
08_marg79: The Gabaonites signify those who believe and seem to be devoted toward the servants of God or to have zeal for the Church, yet have no amendment or devotion or renewal in their morals. Such show only a certain sign of salvation within the Church for a time; but among the spiritual, that is, among the saints of God, they do not obtain the eternal kingdom or freedom.
08_interl136: he who seeks the friendship of Jesus [must bear] the enmities of many patiently; whence: "Son, when thou comest to the service of God, prepare thy soul for temptation"
08_marg80: When the soul joins itself to the word of God, at once it suffers as enemies those whom before it had as friends, and not only men but also the opposing powers. Let him know, then, who seeks the friendship of Jesus, that he must bear the enmities of many. Whence: "All that will live godly in Christ shall suffer persecution", etc. And elsewhere: "Son, when thou comest to the service of God, prepare thy soul for temptation." The Gabaonites too are assailed for the friendship of Jesus, though they are hewers of wood and carriers of water: that is, though thou be last in merits in the Church, yet by this very thing, that thou belongest to Jesus, thou art assailed by five kings. But the Gabaonites are neither abandoned nor spurned by Jesus or by the leaders and elders of the Israelites; but help is brought to their weakness. And this is done in us; whence: "Comfort the feeble-minded, support the weak"; likewise: "You that are stronger bear the infirmities of the weak." So, then, Jesus with the leaders and princes is present to those who are assailed by the opposing powers for his name. And not only does he give help in the war, but he also lengthens the day and the spaces of light and drives off the coming of night.
08_marg81: AUGUSTINE. It is asked how the king of Jerusalem, Adonibezec, and the others with whom he besieged the Gabaonites, are according to the Seventy first [called] kings of the Jebusites, when they came together against them, but afterwards are called kings of the Amorrhites by the Gabaonites themselves, when they sent messengers to Jesus to come to their help. But as we have looked into it, according to the Hebrew they are called in both places [kings] of the Amorrhites; since it is certain that the king of Jerusalem, which was called Jebus, as the metropolis of that nation, was a Jebusite, and Scripture records seven nations to be exterminated, one of which is said to be of the Amorrhites. Unless perhaps this name was universal of all, or rather of the greater part, so that not one but several of these seven were reckoned under this name, although there was one of the seven which was properly called of the Amorrhites. So there is a certain part which is properly called Libya, although this name befits the whole of Africa; and a certain part which is properly called Asia, although some have reckoned Asia half the world, others a third part. The Chanaanites also are mentioned as one nation among those seven, and yet the whole of that land is originally called the land of Chanaan.
08_marg82: AUGUSTINE. When the Gabaonites, besieged by the kings of the Amorrhites, had sent to Jesus to come to their help, Jesus went up from Galgal, he and all the people of warriors with him, all mighty in strength; and the Lord said to Jesus: "Fear them not, for I have delivered them into thy hands; none of them shall stand", etc. Where the Lord was not even consulted whether they should go to them, but of his own accord he foretold the coming victory to his own, who rightly wished to bring help. So he could have been moved, unconsulted, against the Gabaonites when they lied, had not that oath pleased him which compelled them to spare those made subject. For they had believed God concerning what they had heard he promised to his people, that he would overthrow those nations and they would obtain their land; and this faith of theirs he in a manner rewarded, because he did not betray them.
08_marg83: THE SUN AGAINST GABAON. ADAMANTIUS. We wish, if we can, to show how our Lord Jesus Christ prolonged the light and made the day longer, whether for the salvation of men or for the destruction of the opposing powers. From the time the Saviour came, it was the end of the world; in short, he says: "Do penance, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand." But he held back and checked the day of consummation. For God the Father, seeing that the salvation of the nations could stand through him alone, says to him: "Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance", etc. While, then, the Father's promise is being fulfilled and the Church grows and the fulness of the Gentiles comes in, that at last all Israel may be saved, the day is lengthened and the setting is put off; nor does the sun ever go down, but it is always rising, while the sun of justice pours the light of truth into the hearts of believers. But when the measure of believers is fulfilled, and the worse and faded age of the last generation has come, and, iniquity abounding, the charity of many grows cold, and faith is found in few, then the days will be shortened. The same Lord, then, willed to lengthen the day when it is the time of salvation, and to shorten it in the time of tribulation and perdition; while, then, he lengthens the space of light, so let us walk honestly as in the day.
08_interl139: namely, of justice, which knows no setting
08_interl142: Christ, pouring in the light of truth
08_interl144: because he is always rising for the faithful
08_interl145: So, while we fight against the demons, the sun of justice stands by us, who says: "I am with you even to the consummation of the world."
08_interl146: immersed in the five senses of the body and in earthly deeds
08_marg84: ADAMANTIUS. What is it that he says there were five kings, and that these fled into a cave? There is a twofold fight for Christians: for the perfect, such as Paul was and the Ephesians, as he himself says: "Our wrestling is not against flesh and blood, but against principalities and powers, against the rulers of darkness"; but for the lower, against flesh and blood: those, namely, who are still assailed by carnal vices and frailties; which I think is indicated in this place too. For war was declared on the Gabaonites by five kings: on those, that is, who are imperfect, by the five bodily senses; for through some one of these each must needs fall into sin. These five kings assail the Gabaonites, that is, carnal men. And that they are said to have fled into caves can perhaps indicate this, since a cave is a place dug into the depth of the earth: the sense is that when, set in the body, they have sunk themselves in earthly deeds, and have done nothing for the work of God but all for the service of the body, they are said to have fled into caves. Yet it must be known that the very kingdoms whose kings are now conquered by Jesus and flee into caves afterwards come into the lots of the saints and are called the portion of the Lord, as the kingdom of Jerusalem or Lachis or Hebron. In which it is indicated that when the five senses set in the body have been conquered through Jesus, and unbelief has departed from them, and they have died to sin, the soul afterwards uses them as ministers to do the works of justice. So it comes about that in Jerusalem, where a most wicked king reigned, afterwards David, mighty of hand, reigns, or Solomon the peaceful king. For malignant powers sit by or stand by the bodily senses, to solicit the soul to concupiscences and to render foul services; if the faith of Christ has overcome them and they have been hanged on the wood of his cross, these being slain and driven from the kingdom, then the soul is made a portion of God, and Jerusalem the kingdom of God, and a temple is built in it to the Lord. Whence: "For we ourselves also were some time unwise, incredulous, erring, slaves to divers desires and pleasures", etc. For this is Jerusalem's having once been under king Adonibezec, or other cities under other kings.
08_marg85: Jesus killed the enemies not teaching cruelty, as the heretics think, but designating future sacraments in them: that when he destroyed the kings who hold the kingdom of sin in us, as we have yielded our members to serve iniquity unto iniquity, so we may yield them to serve justice unto sanctification. This too is blamed as cruel, that Jesus says: "Put your feet upon their necks and kill them." But this is not cruelty; rather it is found to be humanity and kindness. Would that thou too mightest put thy feet upon serpents and scorpions and upon all the power of the enemy, and tread down the dragon and the basilisk that once reigned in thee, that, all being slain that reigned in thee by the work of sin, Jesus Christ alone may reign in thee.
08_interl148: the opposing powers that stand by the senses
08_marg86: BUT STAY YOU NOT, etc. ADAMANTIUS. The wars of Jesus and the slaughter of kings and enemies are a shadow of heavenly things: namely, of the wars which Jesus Christ wages with his army and his majesties [so the edition], that is, the people of believers, and their leaders, against the devil and his angels. For it is he who in Paul and in the Ephesians "fights against the rulers of darkness". And see, heretic, how the new agrees with the old. To the ancients was promised the kingdom of the holy land flowing with milk and honey, which was then inhabited by most wicked inhabitants and kings. Jesus comes into this land with his army, and with the Israelite leaders he takes it by storm, slays all and holds it, and for the merit of victory receives their kingdoms. To thee through the Gospel are promised not the kingdoms of the earth but of heaven. Nor are they empty; for they have inhabitants, sinners and demons, against whom the apostolic trumpet urges thee to battle. And as there Jesus said that the war would be against the Amorrhites, Pherezites, Hevites and Jebusites, so here too Paul says: "Our wrestling is not against flesh and blood": that is, we shall not fight as the ancients did, nor must we wage battles on earth with men, "but against principalities and powers, against the rulers of the world of this darkness". Now thou understandest in what places these contests are to be stirred up for thee; or, if thou dost not understand, hear more plainly: "against the spirits of wickedness in high places". Thou hast heard who must be driven by thee in war from the heavenly places, that thou mayst take by lot the places of the kingdom of heaven for thy inheritance. This too the Lord says in the Gospel: "From the days of John the kingdom of heaven suffereth violence, and the violent bear it away." Canst thou then likewise bring a charge against our Saviour, that is, of driving out the possessor violently and plundering the possession? Why then do you accuse what Jesus the successor of Moses did? And would that Jesus might open to us the treasure of his wisdom, that we might see of which of the heavenly spiritual enemies that assail Israel that prince of Maceda bore the figure, and he of Lachis, and he of Lebna; or of what vice or error within me, by which the soul is entangled, each of those bears the form whom the people of God slew under the leadership of Jesus: those, namely, who hear his commandments, to whom he gives the power to tread upon serpents and scorpions and all the power of the enemy. Let us pray, then, that our feet may be so beautiful and so strong that they may tread on the necks of the enemies, and so tread down the head of the serpent that it cannot bite our heel. For he who fights under Jesus as leader ought to merit what is written of those warriors: "And all the people returned to Jesus safe, and not one of the children of Israel muttered with his tongue." For he who serves under Jesus ought to return safe from the battle, and receive no wound from the fiery darts of the wicked one, nor be polluted in heart or thought.
08_marg87: And that he adds that no one muttered with his tongue seems to be said because no one boasted of the victory nor ascribed it to his own strength. For they know that Jesus gave the victory; whence: "Yet not I, but the grace of God with me"; and elsewhere: "When you shall have done all these things, say: We are unprofitable servants." Would that my Lord Jesus would grant me to tread down the spirit of fornication and the neck of the spirit of anger and of fury, and the demon of avarice, and boasting, and to crush with my feet the spirit of pride; and when I have done these things, to hang the sum of the work done not on myself but on his cross, according to that: "By whom the world is crucified to me", etc.; "yet not I, but his grace which is in me". If I do this, there will be said to me what the ancient Jesus says: "Do manfully and be of good heart; fear not, neither be ye dismayed at their sight; for the Lord God" hath delivered all your enemies into your hands.
08_marg88: "All these things happened to them in figure, and they are written for us." When he who is a Jew outwardly and circumcised in the flesh reads these things, he thinks only wars are described, and the destruction of enemies, and that the Israelites under the leadership of Jesus conquered and plundered the kingdoms of the nations. But he who is a Jew inwardly, that is, the Christian, who follows Jesus not the son of Nave but the Son of God, understands that these are mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, and says that even now Jesus fights against the opposing powers and casts them out of the cities they possessed, that is, our souls, and kills the kings who reigned in our souls, that sin may reign in us no more; that, the law of sin being shut out, our soul may become the city of God, and God may reign in it, and it may be said to us: "Behold, the kingdom of God is within you." That, then, is mercy which seems cruelty to the heretics, which Jesus Christ fulfils or has fulfilled through the several cities, that is, the souls of believers: that those which were possessed by most wicked kings, these being driven out and slain, he may deign to make the dwelling of God and the temple of the Holy Ghost, and the members that had served iniquity may serve justice. So, then, understand that Jesus killed the king of Jericho, and the king of Hai, and the king of Lebna, and the king of Lachis, and the king of Hebron, so that all the souls which under the most wicked kings kept the law of sin may now live under the laws of God.
08_marg89: LEBNA too is interpreted whiteness, which is understood in different ways. For there is the whiteness of leprosy and the whiteness of light. And Lebna had the whiteness of leprosy under wicked kings; but when it came to the Israelite people it received the whiteness of light.
08_marg90: LACHIS also is interpreted way, which is both praiseworthy in the Scriptures and blameworthy; whence: "The way of the wicked shall perish"; and elsewhere: "Make straight steps for your feet." First, then, the city of Lachis was the way of the wicked; when that was destroyed, afterwards, the Israelites reigning, it came to the right way.
08_marg91: HEBRON: joining, or marriage. The joining of our soul was first with that most wicked husband, the devil; when he died, it was freed from the law of the former, and joined to a good and lawful husband, of whom Paul says: "I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ." So, then, the meaning of these very names accords with the twofold state; so it is better to understand the Israelite wars and the overthrow of cities and kingdoms; so Jesus appears the more religious in having overthrown each city, so that nothing was left in them that breathed, nor any who was saved, nor any who escaped: so that, namely, no sense of malice may breathe again in the soul, nor any feeling of anger or concupiscence be saved; let there be no evil word to escape from the mouth. So the cities of Juda are built; for even now Jesus destroys and builds the soul of each. For the first work of God is to root out evils, the thorns and briers of the vices; for while they occupy the land, it cannot receive the holy seeds. It is necessary, then, first to root out the plant of sin, which the heavenly Father did not plant, and to burn it with fire. The second work is to plant. Moses says that God planted a paradise; but even now he plants in the souls of believers. For in the soul from which he has cut out anger he plants meekness; from which he has cut out pride, he plants humility; from which he roots out wantonness, he plants chastity; ignorance being uprooted, he plants knowledge. Such is said to be the planting of God, rather than [that] of senseless trees. For it is first the work of the word of God to destroy the devilish buildings. For he builds in each one the towers of pride and the walls of haughtiness, which the word of God destroys, that we may be made God's husbandry and God's building, set upon the foundations of the apostles and prophets, and may merit to be made heirs of the holy land, in the Israelite portion, our enemies being destroyed.

08_marg92: AND WHEN HE HAD HEARD. ADAMANTIUS. When Israel according to the flesh read these writings before the coming of Christ, understanding nothing in them but wars, it was sharpened to ferocity by the shedding of blood and fed on wars and seditions. But after the presence of Jesus Christ poured in the light of knowledge, since he is our peace, he teaches peace, the casting down of wars; for peace is restored to the soul if the enemies, namely sins and vices, are driven out of it. Therefore, according to the teaching of Jesus Christ, when we read these things we are armed and roused to battle, but against the enemies that proceed from our heart, namely evil thoughts, thefts, false witness and the like, that we may leave none to be saved or to breathe. For when these are conquered we shall conquer also the powers of the air, and drive them from their kingdom, which they had set up among us on the seats of the vices. Above, the king of Jerusalem gathered four kings with him against Jesus, otherwise Josue, and against the children of Israel. But now not one gathers four or five, but an exceeding multitude. Whence: "But when Jabin king of Asor heard, he sent to Jobab king of the Amorrhites", etc. You see how many of the opposing powers are stirred up against Jesus and the people of God out of the soul. For these demons, before the coming of Christ, reigned quiet and secure, possessing souls. But when the grace and mercy of the Saviour appeared and taught to live godly and holily, that the soul too might take up its freedom and the image of God, for this cause the old possessors are provoked to the fight; and if the first are overwhelmed, many more rise up and conspire in evil; and if the second are conquered, others more wicked rise; and perhaps the more the people of God is increased and multiplied, the more of them conspire to assail it. For the first and author of the war, who invites the rest to the conspiracy, is Jabin king of Asor. Jabin is interpreted sense or prudence. Of this sense Isaias: "And I will bring upon thee the great sense, the prince of the Assyrians, who said: By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom; I have removed the bounds of the nations", etc. The serpent too in paradise is written to have been more prudent than all the beasts, and the unjust steward is said to have done prudently. Asor is interpreted court. The whole earth, then, is the court of this king, who is the devil. Whence it is written in the Gospel that the strong man is in his court, sleeping secure, until a stronger comes who binds him and takes away what he possesses. He sends to Jobab and to the king of Madon. Jobab is interpreted enmities, Madon bitternesses. The devil therefore sends to another hostile power, which is the king of bitternesses, by whose authorship, namely, all bitternesses are inflicted on wretched mortals: the various kinds, namely, of sin. For nothing is more bitter than sin, even if some things seem sweet at first; whence Solomon: "In the end thou shalt find it more bitter than gall", etc. But justice seems bitter at first; at the end it is sweeter than honey, when it has borne the fruit of virtue. The devil therefore sent to Jobab, the enemy, king of bitterness. He sent also to the king of Semeron, which is interpreted hearing. And hearing is twofold: either when God hears man (whence also the patriarch Simeon received his name, because God heard his mother's prayer), or when man hearkens to the command of the devil, who says: If falling down thou wilt adore me, I will give thee all these things. But he who follows Jesus says to him: I will adore the Lord God, and him only will I serve. Those hearken to him who are on his side; as this Semeron, hearkening to him, comes to battle against Jesus. He sends also to the king of Ziph, which is interpreted: how it flows! by way of wonder, namely; for it is to be wondered at how all the things of this world flow away, which among unbelievers are thought to abide. But he who considers the nature of things and the passing of all worldly things says: How it flows!
08_marg93: The devil calls against the children of Israel those also who are over against great Sidon. I indeed have sometimes stayed in the regions of Sidon; I did not find that there are two Sidons, one small and the other great, so far as concerns the earthly place. But Sidon is interpreted huntress, or hunters, namely of demons, of whom there are many differences. Some are hunters in great sins, others in small. When the soul is deceived in the delights of the flesh, it is said to be caught in a small [thing]; but when it denies the providence of God, or worships demons as God, it is deceived in a great one. He sends also to the mountains: this is every sense that exalts and lifts itself against the knowledge of God. He sends also to Araba, that is, ambushes. For he hints at the ensnaring powers, which deceive human souls not by force nor openly, but by unforeseen ambushes; whence: he lieth in wait in secret, as it were "in his den, he lieth in wait to catch the poor", etc. Of which Paul says: "For we are not ignorant of his devices."
08_marg94: He sends also into Ceneroth, which is interpreted as it were lamps, not lamps. For a lamp is one thing, as it were a lamp another. John was a burning lamp, because he was an angel of light. As it were a lamp is he who transforms himself into an angel of light. They too who teach the Catholic faith in the Church, and enlighten the people of God with the word of truth, are burning lamps. But those who, for heretical doctrines, use the testimonies of holy Scripture and false assertions are not lamps, but as it were lamps. He sent also to the plains: to those, namely, who are in the plains and savour lowly and earthly things. He sent also into Nephthed Dor, which is interpreted conversion. And conversion is understood as twofold: that by which one turns to him, either from God to good things [so the edition], or that by which king Jabin, that is, the devil, turns souls to himself. He sends also to those who were in the places by the sea, to the Chanaanites near the waves, which is interpreted as it were stirred up, that is, who disturb all things with commotions and waves; and to the Amorrhites of the sea, that is, the embittering, who indeed inflict bitternesses. Such is the roll of the army of the invisible enemies, who are gathered through king Jabin to assail us who follow Jesus our Saviour. But the Lord says: "Be not afraid of their face", etc.
08_interl171: this is every sense that exalts itself against the knowledge of God
08_interl173: who savour human and earthly things
08_interl174: who are in the flux of this world
08_interl175: as it were stirred up, who, namely, stirs up all things
08_interl176: the embittering, by whose authorship, namely, bitternesses are sent in

08_marg95: FOR TOMORROW AT THIS SAME HOUR. ADAMANTIUS. I see that today we cannot overwhelm all of them, nor kill all; they will be destroyed tomorrow, that is, after the consummation of the world, when it will be said to them: Go into the everlasting fire which God hath prepared for the devil and his angels. For then, if we conquer, following Jesus as leader, we shall receive the kingdom which God has prepared for his saints through Jesus Christ.
08_marg96: Unless these wars bore the figure of spiritual ones, the apostles would never have handed them down to be read by the disciples of Christ, who came to teach peace. For Jesus says: "My peace I give unto you", etc. And the Apostle: "Not revenging yourselves, my dearly beloved", etc. Knowing that carnal wars are no longer to be waged by us, but [wars] against the spirits of wickedness, he commands the soldiers of Christ like a master of warfare: "Put you on the armour of God, that you may be able to stand against the deceits of the devil." And of spiritual wars we have examples from the deeds of the ancients, that we may be spiritual, hearing that the law is spiritual, comparing spiritual things with spiritual, considering from these nations which visibly assailed carnal Israel how many are the nations of opposing powers that fight against the Church of God to make it sin. For as the body, receiving a wound from iron, dies, so the soul wounded by sin. Jesus therefore did as the Lord commanded.
08_marg97: This, then, Jesus fulfilled according to the command of God. But if any of the enemies had survived, the horses would have had to be hamstrung, lest any of them should flee away. But since none was left that breathed, why are the horses hamstrung, which could have been of use to the victors? For the Israelites were wont, when their enemies were conquered, to keep the beasts for use, as when the Madianites were conquered they kept some thousands of asses. Nor is it written of the asses that they were hamstrung, nor are the spoils or animals of the Madianites said to have been killed, but kept for use. But because these had not asses but horses, the Lord himself commanded them to be hamstrung. Do we think this happened by chance, that the horses were killed and the asses kept, and that anything befalls by chance in the commands of God? In short, the children of Israel are never recorded to have used horses. The law also commands nothing about horses, but about asses, as about animals that are for the labours and burdens of men; for by horses wars are waged. For the horse is an animal of wanton motion and proud neck; but asses frequently signify the Gentiles, which the Saviour himself shows, sitting upon an ass, who is never recorded to have sat upon a horse; and sending the disciples to loose the ass and the colt he says: Say that the Lord hath need of it; and sitting upon it he enters Jerusalem. Whence: "Behold thy king, meek, sitting upon a beast of burden and a young colt of an ass; and he will destroy the chariot out of Ephraim and the horse out of Jerusalem." He then who sits upon an ass destroys the chariots of Ephraim and the horse of Jerusalem. The horses and chariots that are destroyed signify those who fell from heaven through pride and wantonness, when either they offered themselves as kindlers of lust for the daughters of men, or followed him who said: "I will set my seat above the clouds, and I will be like the most High." Hence perhaps it is said: "Vain is the horse for safety"; and of those who trusted in demons: "Some trust in chariots, and some in horses; but we will call upon the name of the Lord our God." For he would not have compared chariots and horses with God as to invoking; but the nations fighting against Israel invoked the demons, the horses. And the nations coming to the faith, which are signified by the asses, are rightly kept; but by the horses and chariots the demons, the enemies of human salvation, are rightly destroyed. The passions of the body too, that is, lust, pride, wantonness and levity, on which the unhappy soul is carried as on horseback to the precipices, can be understood by the horses and chariots which are commanded to be hamstrung. For the horse is hamstrung when the body is humbled by abstinence; and the chariots are burned with fire when that is fulfilled: "I am come to cast fire on the earth", etc., of which it is said: "Was not our heart burning within us", etc. Therefore, then, the horse is called vain for safety, if the motions of our body are carried away unbridled and not restrained by the yoke of abstinence. But if anyone is stung and pricked to the heart by the words of God that we speak, and he who yesterday was carried like a horse into lust today repents, is converted and embraces a chaste life, we shall seem to have hamstrung the horses with the sword of the word of God. And whose horses are hamstrung? Those of Jabin, namely, which is interpreted prudence or sense: of him, namely, of whom it is said that "the wisdom of the flesh is an enemy to God"; and elsewhere: "Puffed up by the sense of his flesh." Jabin was king of Asor, which is interpreted court, and is said to have held the principality of all the kingdoms. In this court the prince of this world reigns, that is, over the earth, or rather in the vices of the flesh. The horses also of all those kings whose force we have expounded according to their names were killed by Jesus; whose vices we who serve under Jesus ought to cut off in ourselves, and to hamstring with the spiritual sword all the cavalry of the vices; we ought also to burn the chariots, that is, to cut away from us every spirit of haughtiness.
08_marg98: Let us fulfil in ourselves also what is said, that none be left that breathes. If anger rises in thy heart, perhaps thou wilt not fulfil its works, whether from fear of men or from fear of the judge to come. But this is not enough; not even the very stirring of anger ought to have place in thee. The very disturbance is unbecoming in one who serves under Jesus as leader. The same is to be thought of all the vices: that nothing of them breathe at all in the heart; lest perhaps, if the habit or thought of some small vice be left, it grow strong in the course of time and, lying hidden, gradually gather strength, and at last bring one back to the vomit, and the last state become worse than the first. Whence: blessed is he that taketh and dasheth the little ones, namely, against the rock, [the little ones] of Babylon, namely the evil thoughts which confound and disturb the heart; which, at the beginning, while they are small, are to be seized and dashed against the rock, which is Christ, and at his command slain, that nothing may remain in us that breathes.
