08_marg99: AS MOSES APPOINTED HIM, etc. "This is the word of the law, according to that: They have Moses and the prophets; let them hear them." The law therefore commanded us to kill all the kings of sin who provoke us to sin. So Jesus did, nor did he transgress anything. For it is he who destroys the vices in us and the kingdoms of sin. Christ himself also did all that Moses commanded in the law. Whence: "God sent his Son, made of a woman, made under the law", etc. For he fulfilled all that the law commanded, that he might redeem us from the curse of the law; who says: "I am not come to destroy the law, but to fulfil."
08_interl185: because he came not to destroy the law, but to fulfil
08_marg100: AUGUSTINE. It is not to be thought cruelty that Jesus left no one alive in the cities delivered to him, because God had commanded this. But those who think from this that God himself was cruel, and therefore will not believe that the true God was the author of the Old Testament, judge as perversely of the works of God as of the sins of men, not knowing what each deserves, and thinking it a great evil when things that are to fall are cast down and mortals die.
08_interl186: of sin, namely, that sin may not reign in us
08_marg101: AND ALL THEIR KINGS HE TOOK AND SMOTE. ADAMANTIUS. Sin reigned in all of us, and there was in all a general kingdom of sin. Whence: "For all have sinned, and do need the glory of God." For each one had in himself a spiritual king: either avarice, or pride, or lying, or the like. Whence Paul says: "Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body", etc. But after Jesus came he killed all the kings who reigned in us, and commanded all to be killed; for he who keeps any alive in himself cannot be in the army of Jesus. If avarice, boasting, lust, pride or the like reigns in thee, thou art not an Israelite soldier, nor dost thou fulfil the command which the Lord gave to Jesus.
08_marg102: AUGUSTINE. It is asked how this is true, since neither afterwards in the time of the Judges nor of the Kings could the Hebrews take all the cities of those seven nations without exception. But either it is to be understood thus, that Jesus approached no city in war which he did not take; or certainly that none of them was taken but of those that were in the regions mentioned above. For the regions are enumerated in which were the cities of which this conclusion was made: and he took all in war.
08_marg103: "And Jesus took in war all who had come out to war." For Jesus is superior to all, because it was brought about by God that they were emboldened and came out against Israel to battle. He did not say that Jesus took some in war and some not, but he took all and destroyed them. For the Lord Jesus purged all the kinds of sin and destroyed them all. For we were all unwise, incredulous, erring, serving divers desires and any sins whatever. Jesus therefore killed all who had come out to war. For Jesus, the Word of God and the Wisdom of the Father, is superior to all; whence Paul says: "And such some of you were; but you are washed, but you are justified in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ." So, then, he took and destroyed all, because it was brought about by the Lord that their heart was emboldened and they came out to battle against Israel, that they might be exterminated. For as long as the hostile powers which work sins in us do not come, nor provoke us to fight or to struggle, they cannot be killed nor exterminated. Therefore God is said to permit, nay almost to stir up, the adversary powers to come against us in battle, that we may conquer and they may perish. Their number seems to me infinite, because with almost each single man there are some spirits who contrive the different kinds of sins. There is a spirit of fornication, there is a spirit of anger, there is another of avarice, another of pride; and if it happen that there is someone who is driven by all these evils, or even by more, he is to be thought to have all these, or even more, spirits in him. Whence there are to be believed to be many with each, because single men have not single vices but many. Nor is it to be thought that one spirit of fornication seduces him who commits fornication in Britain and him who does so in India or in other places; nor that there is one spirit of anger which drives different men in different places. But I think rather that there is one spirit of fornication and innumerable ones who obey him in this office, and with each man different spirits serving under that prince, who solicit them to sins of this kind. Similarly I think there is one prince of anger and innumerable ones under him; and the same is to be thought of the other sins. Therefore not one principality is spoken of by the Apostle, but many, against whom we have to fight.
08_marg104: Yet I think there is a prince of all these, more eminent in wickedness and stronger in crime, who, as the leader of all the princes and the master of the whole army, drives the whole world, which these solicit one by one; who is signified by Jabin. And I think that the saints, fighting against these instigators of sins and conquering them one by one, diminish the army of the demons, and as it were kill very many horses. For example, if one who by living chastely has overcome the spirit of fornication, it is no longer lawful for that spirit which was overcome by him to assail another man; but, like that spirit which asked Jesus not to be sent into the abyss, it seems to follow that each one, conquered, is led away either into the abyss, or into the exterior darkness, or into a place worthy of him, by the just judge Christ. And hence it is that, a very great number of demons being now conquered, the Gentiles are let come to the faith. But if it seems hard to anyone, or fabulous, that very many demons are in single sinners, let him return to the authority of the Gospel, and he will find that the demoniac who dwelt in the tombs, when he was asked by Christ, What is thy name?, answered, Legion. What wonder, then, if single demons are ascribed to the single kinds of sins, when it is written that a whole legion was in one man? There are, then, in their hands two-edged swords, which destroy the opposing powers. Hence Paul says: "The God of peace crush Satan under your feet speedily." For if Satan is one, how can he have been crushed and work again? Perhaps, then, there are to be thought as many Satans as there are who do his works. Whence it seems to be said in Wisdom too "that the wicked man, cursing Satan, curseth his own soul". In the little book also which is called the Testament of the Twelve Patriarchs, which is not held in the canon, I found that by single sinners single Satans ought to be understood. Moreover, Satan is called adversary; all, then, who oppose the will of God can be called Satans. Blessed then is he who, holding the spiritual sword, does not take it away from the necks of these enemies. Whence Jeremias: "Cursed be he that doth the work of God deceitfully, and that withholdeth his sword from blood" of the wicked. If we understand this according to the letter, we must needs shed blood unceasingly; which the Jews thinking, become cruel and swift to shed blood. But let us not take away the sword of the word of God from the blood of the opposing powers, which are slain when we do not do their works.
08_marg105: "Because it was brought about by the Lord that their heart was emboldened, so that they went out to war against Israel, that they might be exterminated, so that no mercy was given them, but they were exterminated, as the Lord said to Moses", etc. It is said, "by the Lord to be emboldened", that is, their heart to be hardened, as of Pharao; that this is done by divine and deep judgment is not to be doubted, when God forsakes and the enemy takes charge; which is to be taken here as there. But here something else stirs us: how it is said that the heart was emboldened to this end, that they rose up to war against Israel, and therefore were not shown mercy, although [it would be] against God's command. It must be understood to have been said to this end, that these fought in such a way that they were not spared, nor were the Israelites, neglecting God's command, bent to mercy by them. Which indeed is not to be believed could have happened under the leadership of Jesus, who diligently kept the precepts of God. But neither would he have destroyed them so quickly unless they had come against him in closest conspiracy; and so it could happen that, if they had not been overthrown by him who took care to fulfil the precepts of God, they would have remained until that time when they could be spared. After the death of Jesus they spared them, only subjecting them to their rule; and some they could not even conquer. But these things were not done under his leadership, but when, now old, he was resting from war, only dividing the land to them, so that they themselves, without him making war, took the lands divided to them partly by fighting.
08_interl187: For the demons are permitted by the Lord, or rather stirred up, to come against us in battle, that we may conquer and they may perish.
08_interl188: not the son of Nave, who held Judea alone, but Jesus Christ, to whom the multitude of believers runs together from every land and every nation
08_marg106: Not under Jesus son of Nave, under whom it hardly ever ceased from wars, but under Jesus Christ. For thou hast come to Jesus and in baptism obtained the remission of sins, and now in thee the flesh does not fight against the spirit and the spirit against the flesh. Thy land, then, has ceased from wars, if only thou bear about the death of Jesus in thy body, that, all battles in thee ceasing, thou mayst be made a true peacemaker and be called a son of God. But this will be when thou hast gone through the wars and subdued the adversaries; then thou shalt rest under thy vine, which is Christ, and under thy fig tree, which is the Holy Ghost.
08_interl189: Jesus Christ, the beginning and "the firstborn of every creature"
08_interl190: advanced from "the evil days", and few, to the eternal days
08_marg107: JOSUE WAS OLD, etc. Thou art grown old and advanced in age. ADAMANTIUS. Priests and elders are so called not for long life, but for ripeness of sense and the gravity of a life to be revered, especially when "full of days" is added. For if anyone were called a priest or elder for length [of years], the first Adam, or Mathusala, or Noe, who lived longer than the rest, would be ranked by this name. But Abraham, who lived less, is the first in the Scriptures to be called a priest or elder. For the Lord said to Moses: "Choose thee out of all the people elders whom thou thyself knowest" to be elders. Observe too whether anywhere you find a sinner called an elder and "full of days". Now therefore it is the voice of the Holy Ghost declaring Jesus an elder and advanced in days, which cannot be said of sinners. For the sinner is not advanced in days; for he does not stretch himself forth to the things that are before, but always turns back to his vomit. And therefore he is not fit for the kingdom of heaven. The Lord, then, was not speaking to Jesus of old age, which all saw and knew, but by this a great testimony of mystery was given to the son of Nave. For as this sun makes days for this world, so the Sun of justice makes spiritual days, which are lit by the brightness of truth and knowledge. If anyone, then, passes in the precepts of God this present life, which, as Jacob says, is of few and evil days, and keeps himself unspotted from this world, and subdues all his spiritual enemies, he will be advanced from these few and evil days to the eternal days, marked by the light of the eternal Sun. So, then, Jesus is said by the divine answer to be advanced in days.
08_marg108: But who is so an elder and senior advanced in days as Jesus Christ, who is the beginning and the firstborn of every creature? Therefore perhaps he alone is truly called an elder, before whom there is none. Even if there are those who are called priests or elders or pontiffs, yet he, as among pontiffs he is the prince of pontiffs, so among priests or elders he is the prince of priests, as he is prince among all, because he is the head of all.
08_interl191: by passing over to the eternal days
08_interl192: whence: "Until I make thy enemies thy footstool"
08_marg109: AND A VERY LARGE LAND IS LEFT. Another reading: And the land that is left is very much. Above it was said that the land ceased from wars, and that Jesus took all the land; yet it is not to be thought that Scripture is contrary to itself. For in the spiritual understanding you will find nothing contrary. Look at the first coming of our Saviour, when he came to sow the seed, or his word: for he took all the land by the mere casting of the seed, and put to flight the opposing powers which had besieged the minds of the Gentiles, and sowed the word, and spread the churches. This is his first possession of the whole land. See how he takes the land also a second time, which is now said to be left in great part. For Paul says of him: "For he must reign, until he hath put [all his] enemies [under his feet as] a footstool", etc. This is the land which is now said to be left, until all things without exception are made subject under his feet.
08_marg110: THIS IS THE LAND THAT IS LEFT. All the borders of the Philistines, and the rest that follow. Many things remain which we see not yet subjected, all of which must be subjected. For there can be no end unless all things have been subjected to him. Whence all nations shall serve him. In the second coming, then, Jesus will obtain this great land. But blessed are they who were obtained at his first coming. For these will come into grace who, while many adversaries resist, receive the inheritance of the land of promise by war and arms. But he who will be subjected of necessity, when the last enemy, death, shall be destroyed, will not be in grace.
08_interl193: Sidonians, that is, hunters, of whom it is said: "Our soul hath been delivered as a sparrow out of the snare of the fowlers."
08_marg111: I AM [HE]. ADAMANTIUS. When Jesus had enumerated very many nations, of the Sidonians alone he said: And all the Sidonians I will exterminate from the face of the children of Israel. Sidonians are interpreted hunters. These are the demons of whom the Prophet says: "They prepared a snare for my feet." These the Lord exterminates, that there be none to spread snares and nets to deceive souls, and that every one may rest under his vine and under his fig tree.
08_marg112: AND NOW DIVIDE. After this it is read that Moses gave an inheritance to some, and afterwards Jesus, according to the command of the Lord, distributed the inheritance. By Moses understand the law: those who lived according to the law received the inheritance first, but outside the land of promise. And when they had received it, they do not possess it nor divide it among themselves, but wait until it be distributed to them by lot through Jesus. Hence the Apostle says: All these, being approved by the testimony of faith, received not the promises, God providing some better thing for us, that they should not be perfected without us. They have therefore their promise already, and have rested, judged worthy through Moses to take their inheritance; but they still fight for those who serve under Jesus. For all the fathers who have slept before us fight with us and help us with their prayers. Whence: That synagogue will lick up this synagogue, as the calf licketh up the green grass of the field. For the synagogue of the Lord that went before us will consume the opposing synagogue with mouth and tongue, that is, it will consume our adversaries with prayers. With prayers, then, and with meditation on the word of God and right sense, we must fight.
08_marg113: ADAMANTIUS. As they who receive the law, which is the shadow of the true law, serve the pattern and shadow of heavenly things, so they who divide the inheritance of the land in Judea follow the pattern and shadow of the heavenly division. For the truth is in heaven, the shadow on earth. While this stood on earth, there was an earthly Jerusalem, and a temple, and an altar, and a visible worship; there were pontiffs and priests, the cities and villages of Judea, and all the things that are written in this book. But when at the coming of Christ the truth, descending from heaven, sprang out of the earth, and justice looked down from heaven, the shadows fell; the altar and the temple fell, so that now there is no place, neither on mount Garizim nor in Jerusalem, where men ought to adore, but the true adorers adore the Father in spirit and in truth. The truth being present, then, the shadow ceased. And when the temple was present which was built in the womb of the virgin by the Spirit of God and the power of the most High, the temple built of stones was destroyed. The high priest of the good things to come is present, and the pontiffs of bulls and goats cease. The Lamb has come that taketh away the sins of the world, and the lamb taken from the flocks ceases, slain to no purpose for so many ages. It followed, then, that, the inheritance of the kingdom of heaven being opened, the earthly inheritance should cease, and, all these ceasing, every mouth should be stopped and all the world be made subject to God. For divine providence ordered all these things to be taken away for this reason, that, the figures ceasing, they might receive a certain way of truth. The whole earthly Jerusalem has been overthrown, but we have the heavenly, which is the mother of all. By the mercy of God, then, the earthly inheritance has been taken from us, that we may seek an inheritance in heaven. And so a first and a second division of the inheritance is related: the first indeed was made through Moses, the second and mightier through Jesus. Moses gave possession beyond the Jordan to Ruben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasses; but all the others receive their inheritance through Jesus.
08_interl194: because he could not say: "Sell all that thou hast and give to the poor", etc. For this is to give a portion to the Levites. For Christ, who said these and such things, gave the Levites a portion.
08_marg114: But neither Moses nor Jesus gave an inheritance to the Levites, because God himself is their inheritance. These perhaps are they who in the Church go before others in strength of soul and grace of merits. These perhaps are they who among the people of the saved give their labour to wisdom and knowledge, and keep their mind pure and cultivate it with all excellent virtues, and teach the simpler how they may come to the Saviour. Their inheritance is the Lord himself, who is the wisdom which they have loved above all things.
08_marg115: TO THE TRIBE OF THE CHILDREN OF RUBEN, etc. Yet I find a certain difference between the things which Moses distributed and those which Jesus [distributed]. For Moses, giving inheritance to two tribes and a half, gave no portion to the Levites. But Jesus, not only in those tribes to which he divided the land, but also in those to which Moses had divided it, decreed dwellings for the Levites in each tribe. For the levitical or priestly order, which spends its labour on the wisdom and knowledge of God, could not receive a lot of habitation from Moses, who was the minister not of the truth but of the shadow and pattern. But our Jesus, who is the wisdom of God, provides dwellings for the wise. Moses could not say: "Sell all that thou hast and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me." This is to give a portion to the Levites. Nor could he say: "He that doth not renounce all that he possesseth cannot be my disciple", nor the other: "Every one that hateth not father and mother and brothers and sisters", etc. Therefore he could not dispense the dwellings of the priests and Levites. Blessed, then, is he who is found worthy to receive from Jesus a lot of the heavenly mansion, of which Jesus says: "Father, I will that where I am, these also may be with me; and as I in thee and thou in me are one, these also may be one in us." Yet those whose inheritance is said to be the wisdom of God, the Word, truth and justice, receive habitation meanwhile with those whose inheritance is on earth, that those who cannot by themselves may through them be made partakers of the wisdom and knowledge of God; and so the divine dispensation reaches to the least, that that may be fulfilled: He that had much had nothing over, and he that had little had no lack. And what the Apostle says: "That your abundance may supply their want", etc. Thus, then, the priest and the Levite, who have no land, are commanded to dwell together [with the Israelites], that the priest and the Levite may receive from the Israelite the earthly things which they have not, and the Israelite from the priest and the Levite the heavenly and divine things which he has not. For the law of God is committed to the priests and Levites, that they may give their labour to this alone and be free for the word of God without any care, sustained by the ministries of the laity. For if [the laity] do not provide them with necessaries, they will be less free for the law of God, being occupied with bodily cares, and the laity will be in peril. For the light of knowledge that is in them will be darkened, thou not supplying oil to the lamp; and by thy fault the blind leading the blind will fall with him into the ditch.
08_marg116: THIS POSSESSION. ADAMANTIUS. Let us learn from the law how necessarily the division of the land is described, which is said [to be made] first through Moses, secondly through Jesus, not that we may keep both, but that, learning the reason of each, we may hold that one alone which is delivered to us by Jesus Christ. That land, then, which is beyond the Jordan Moses distributed; but this which is in the holy land, Jesus and the princes of the tribes. You see that when the true inheritance of the holy land began to be distributed, the princes of the tribes of the true and spiritual Israel are taken up. These are the apostles, to whom it is said: You also shall sit on seats judging the twelve tribes of Israel. The priest too is taken up, that is, the mystical word of God. For so it says, that Jesus and Eleazar came together to divide the land.
08_interl195: who is wisdom and knowledge, to whom alone the Levites and priests give their labour
08_interl196: the hidden and mystical word of God
08_interl198: the apostles, to whom it is said: "You also shall sit judging the twelve tribes of Israel."
08_marg117: ISIDORE. The nations destroyed, Josue divides the land of promise to the peoples by lot; Christ too cast out the nations, that is, the spirits of the errors of the Gentiles, from before the face of his faithful, and divided the land by lot, bestowing on each his own gifts.
08_interl199: lest, occupied with temporal things, they should serve heavenly things the less
08_marg118: ISIDORE. Moses decreed possession beyond the Jordan to two tribes and a half only, but all the rest receive it through Jesus, because more receive the heavenly promises through the faith of Jesus Christ than through the law. For the two and a half tribes figured the former people, which had indeed knowledge of the Trinity, but not perfect. But the nine and a half tribes which receive the promise of the holy land through Jesus signify the new people, which receive from Jesus Christ, through faith and grace, the inheritance of the eternal promise after the laver, as after the crossing of the Jordan. But these too do not reach the number ten, which is as it were perfect, because not even at the coming of the Lord itself were all things perfectly announced to us. Whence: I have yet many things to say to you, but [you cannot bear them now]; but the Spirit of truth, who proceedeth from the Father, will announce to you all things. The perfection, then, and sum of all good things is in the Holy Ghost.
08_marg119: ISIDORE. The Levites do not receive an inheritance of the land, because Jesus Christ is their inheritance, according to that: I am their inheritance, and no possession shall be given them in Israel; for I am their possession. For [he is] the inheritance and possession of the clergy. Therefore God willed it to be said, because they were made the ministers of his altar and [his] lot. Whence also clergy is interpreted lot. Rightly therefore do they possess God for an inheritance who, that they may be able to serve God without hindrance, desire to be poor in spirit, that they may be able to say: The Lord is the portion of my inheritance, etc.
08_marg120: ISIDORE. Jesus decrees dwellings for the Levites throughout all the tribes, that those who in the Church of the Lord give their labour to knowledge and administer the grace of doctrine may receive earthly support from those to whom they dispense divine things. Whence Paul: If we have sown unto you spiritual things, is it a great matter if we reap your carnal things? And rightly are they divided among all the tribes, who live by the dispensation of all.
08_marg121: ADAMANTIUS. Caleb, who is interpreted as it were heart, first receives an inheritance from Jesus. This is he who in all things gives his labour to understanding, who is said to be no other member of the body of the Church than the heart, which is the most excellent thing in us; that is, he who does all things with reason and prudence, and so dispenses to all as if there were no other member but the heart. And Jephone is interpreted conversion. Caleb, then, is the son of conversion. For one converted to God brings forth such fruit from himself, and the heart begets a son. Every one, then, who is free for divine senses and does all things rationally is Caleb. He indeed was instructed first by Moses, secondly by Jesus, beside whom he stood, and says: Thou knowest the word that the Lord spoke to Moses, etc. Who else can know the word that the Lord spoke to Moses but Jesus alone? For none understood the law as Jesus taught it. For he taught and opened all things. He revealed to Paul that the law was spiritual, etc.
08_interl202: Christ alone knew what the Lord spoke to Moses. For none so understood the law. He taught and opened all things.
08_marg122: THOU KNOWEST WHAT THE LORD SPOKE, etc. ADAMANTIUS. This is what the Lord said: If you did believe Moses, you would believe me also; for he wrote of me. And "of me", that is, Caleb, who is the heart, he said; for it is certain that Moses wrote of the heart, because he wrote all things wisely.
08_interl203: Moses, of whom it is said: "For he wrote of me"
08_interl204: "If you did believe Moses, you would believe me also."
08_marg123: AS STRONG, etc. For the saint is equally strong in things present and in things past, in new and in old, in the Gospels and in the law. This, then, is why he now says that he is strong under Jesus as he was then with Moses, because the watchful heart is strong in the mysteries of both testaments.
08_marg124: The saint seeks nothing lowly, nothing cast down, but a high mountain, in which are great and fortified cities, because the wise man takes fortified cities and destroys the strongholds in which the wicked trust.
08_marg125: ADAMANTIUS. The cities and walls are the doctrines of the wicked and the syllogisms of the Prophets [so the edition], by which they build up every impious thing contrary to the divine law. Those too are fortified cities set on mountains, which the heretics place by assertions from the Scriptures as on high mountains. These cities every wise man who preaches the word of truth destroys, and he overturns the cities of falsehood with the ram of truth. So the most wise Caleb, standing before Jesus, promises that he is the stronger for battle, and therefore asks that leave be granted him to dispute with the dialecticians of the world, who confirm false things for true, that he may overturn all that they build with false assertions. Jesus, seeing his eagerness, blesses him who asks and dares such things. Thou too, if thou wilt give thy labour to study and meditate prudently on the law of God and be made a heart in the law of God, canst overturn these great and fortified cities, that is, false assertions, that thou too mayst merit to be blessed by Jesus and to receive Hebron, which is interpreted joining or marriage. By this perhaps can be shown that the double cave bought by the patriarch Abraham is in it, in which lie the marriages of the fathers and their remains, that is, Abraham with Sara, Isaac with Rebecca, Jacob with Lia. Caleb therefore merited to receive the remains of the fathers for an inheritance, because by the wisdom in which he flourished under Moses and Jesus he had understood the reason of the joinings, and what cause there was that with Abraham Sara alone lay there, and neither Agar nor Cetura merited to be joined to him; or why with Jacob Lia alone lay, and neither Rachel, though more loved, nor any of the concubines was coupled with him in the tomb. In the memorials of the fathers, then, wise Caleb takes his inheritance. To him Jesus gives Hebron, the metropolis of the race of the Enacites, and it becomes his lot until this present day. Would that the lot of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob were given to me too, that my God might be made [mine], as he was made the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, in Christ Jesus.
08_interl205: because he asks and dares such things
08_interl206: which is interpreted joining or marriage
08_interl208: If thou wilt have an inheritance from Jesus, the land of thy flesh must rest and not fight against the spirit.
08_marg126: AND THE LAND CEASED FROM, etc. ADAMANTIUS. This is not written in the distribution of Moses, but in the distribution of Jesus. If then thou wilt be made worthy to obtain an inheritance from Jesus, thou must first finish all wars and stand in peace, that it may be said of the land of thy flesh that the land ceased from wars. And whereas it is the custom of holy Scripture to name the four parts of the world, which they call axes or quarters, in the description of the borders of the tribe of Juda only two are named. And the borders, it says, of the children of the tribe of Juda according to their peoples were from the borders of Idumea, from the desert of Sinai, to the west. And when it had described the borders from the west, it says: and from the east the salt sea. But of the north and the south it was silent. The first borders of Judea, then, are the borders of Idumea, which is interpreted earthly; after earthly things, then, the borders of Judea follow at once, but from the desert, it says, of Sinai, that is, of temptations: after temptations, then, follow the borders of the inheritance of Juda. East and west name the neighbouring places of which we spoke above, that is, the confines. The valley of Egypt too is marked as neighbouring the western parts, which is from the desert on the west. But on the east the borders are girt by the salt sea. After this: from the hills, it says, which stretch to the west, and thence it goes up to the west as far as Cadesbarne, and so it stretches from the west to Cades. These are their borders on the side of the Africus, and thence it went on to the valley of Egypt. See how in the parts of the west it names the Africus, Egypt and the setting, that each may know that these must be passed through by him, and so at last he may come to the royal tribe from which our Lord sprang. Now from the borders of Idumea is the desert of Sinai. Therefore it is necessary for us to pass through the desert of temptations, that we may be able to come to the inheritance of the children of Juda. We must also go up the ascent of the hills of Accabim, which is interpreted scorpions, because the scorpions must be passed by us and trodden on, of which it is said: Behold, I have given you power to tread upon scorpions and serpents, etc. Let him, then, who will enter into the inheritance of the tribe of Juda go up these ascents, tread on and escape these scorpions. Perhaps to Ezechiel making this journey the Lord said: Son of man, thou dwellest in the midst of scorpions. And the borders are, it says, as far as Cadesbarne. Cades is interpreted holy or sanctification. The borders of Juda, then, reach as far as sanctification. It is said too that on the eastern side of the tribe of Juda is the salt sea, and after this, in its part, the fountain of the sun and the city of the sun are named; and in the same tribe is also the city of letters. Everyone, therefore, who would enter into the portion of the children of Juda must first pass the salt sea, that is, overcome the waves and whirlwinds of this world, and escape all the things of this world which, for their uncertainty and slipperiness, are compared to the waves of the sea, that he may be able to come to the land of Juda, and to the fountain of the Sun of justice, which is the fountain of water springing up into life everlasting, and afterwards find the city of the Sun of justice. There is in Egypt too a city of the sun, but that took its name from this sun which the heavenly Father commands to rise upon the good and the bad. But that which is in Judea is made [the city] of the saints only, because it is the city of God; and that fountain mentioned above, made a river, maketh the city of God joyful. Thou too, if thou be fortified on every side and girt with the wall of continence, perfected with the towers of patience and magnanimity, shalt be made a city of God. But if to this thou add the light of the knowledge of God, and the Sun of justice shine upon thee, thou shalt be made a city of the sun, or perhaps shalt inherit the city of the sun. And if thou study in the law of God day and night, and the book of the law depart not from thy hand, thy inheritance too shall be made the city of letters.
08_marg127: ADAMANTIUS. Not a little profit is conferred on the soul when the reading of the divine word, even if obscure, glides into our ears. For it is believed by the Gentiles that by certain chants, which they call incantations, those whose art this is, whispering certain compiled names, even names which not even those who invoke them know, by the mere sound of the voice lull serpents to sleep or even draw them out of their holes; and often in human bodies swellings or fevers or other such things are said to be loosed or repressed by the voice alone; and sometimes too a certain stupor of sense is said to be inflicted on the soul, if only the faith of Christ have not resisted. If so, how much more must we believe that any naming whatever of holy Scripture, whether of its words or of its names, is to be held more powerful than every incantation and chant! For as among unbelievers the contrary powers, hearing those names, are present, and also give their labour to that for which they perceive themselves invoked by this or that name, spending the service of their office on the thing to which they have bound themselves, much more do the heavenly powers who are with us gladly receive it if we bring forth from our mouth the words of Scripture and the namings of these names as certain chants and incantations. And even if we do not understand them, those powers understand, and, as if invited by a chant, delight to be present with us and to bring help. For divine powers are not only around us but also within us; whence: Bless the Lord, O my soul, and let all that is within me [bless] his holy name, that is, all things that are within me. It is certain, then, that there are many powers within us, to which the care of our souls or bodies is committed. If they are holy, they are delighted when the Scriptures are read by us, and become stronger toward our diligence, even if our understanding be without fruit; according to that of the Apostle: If we speak with tongues and our spirit prays, but our understanding is without fruit. The Apostle once brought forth a wonderful mystery in this, namely that it can be that the spirit which is in us prays and our understanding is without fruit. For those powers which are given to help our soul are refreshed by the hearing of holy Scripture as by divine and rational foods, when we bring forth from our mouth according to the divine words. Christ himself too, if he find us free for such studies, not only deigns to be refreshed and fed in us, but, if he see these banquets prepared with us, will also bring the Father with him, according to that: I and the Father will come and will make our abode with him. But as by such meditations we call forth the fellowship and services of the divine [powers], so by the namings of such words and names we put to flight the snares of the malignant powers and the assaults of the demons. For example: as one may see a serpent lulled by incantations carried in the hands, or drawn out of its holes, able to do no harm, its poisons benumbed by the power of the incantations, so, by the power of the divine reading, if there be within us any serpent of the contrary power, it is driven out by the chants, if thou bear patiently, that is, if thou turn not away thy hearing for weariness. If, then, an obscure Scripture which thou understandest not is read to thee, receive this profit meanwhile; only take care that thou become not like the deaf asps, which hear not the voice of the charmer and of the wizard that charmeth wisely. For there is a chant that is chanted by the wise Jesus son of Nave and by all the prophets. Let us not, then, be weary of hearing the holy Scriptures, even if we do not understand; but it will be done to us according to our faith, believing that all Scripture divinely inspired is profitable, even if we do not perceive the profit. Physicians sometimes give a food or a drink, for example, to dispel the dimness of the eyes, and yet in eating or drinking we do not perceive that it helps; but when one day and another and a third have passed, in its own time the power of the food or drink, carried by hidden passages to the sight, little by little purges the vision.
08_interl211: of the fruits of the world, namely
08_interl212: "I have given you power to tread upon serpents and scorpions."
08_interl213: "of water springing up into life everlasting"
08_marg128: BUT TO CALEB THE SON OF JEPHONE HE GAVE, etc. ADAMANTIUS. The distribution of Jesus begins from Caleb. For the lot of his portion was given to him before his tribe, that is, the tribe of Juda, received [its own], and not in the outermost parts but in the midst of the children of Juda; and not by lot, but by the command of the Lord, a whole city is given him. For whom else was it fitting to obtain such an inheritance but Caleb, who alone was saved with Jesus out of the six hundred thousand armed men who had gone out of Egypt? And he it is who must receive the metropolis. Therefore Jesus gave him the city of Arboc, the metropolis of Enach, which is Hebron, in which were the memorials of the fathers; and he exterminated from it the three sons of Enach. First, then, let us discuss why Caleb received a metropolis, and that one which is called the first metropolis among all in the land, and the metropolis of Enach, which is interpreted empty humility. Now there are two humilities: one praiseworthy, of which it is said: Learn of me, because I am meek and humble of heart, etc.; and: He that humbleth himself shall be exalted, etc.; and: Be you humbled under the mighty hand of God; the other blameworthy, of which it is said that Ammon humbled Thamar his sister. This is the empty humility which comes down from sin. Caleb took and cut down its metropolis, and killed the three sons of Enach, that is, of empty humility, and dwelt in the city. The first is the son Susi, that is, outside me: this is outside the holy, for the son of empty humility is outside the holy, nay outside God. Another is Achimaau, which is interpreted my brother without counsel. For all the brothers who are born of empty humility are outside counsel. The third is Thalamin, which is interpreted a precipice or suspension, because there is nothing of stability in him, but all things wandering and rushing headlong. These exterminated, he went up into Dabir, whose name before was the city of letters. Now Dabir is interpreted speech. By the city of letters, then, understand the whole instrument of the Old Testament, such as this very scripture which we are expounding, which afterwards is made Dabir, that is, speech. For what before was in letters and was understood according to the letter has now in the churches of Christ been made speech, as they speak of it and discuss it: first the apostles, removing the surface of the letter and bringing it forth into spiritual speech; then the doctors one by one, making of the single letters speech and angelic disputation. And who are the three sons of Enach whom Caleb killed, to whose person we have ascribed the power of the law among earthly things? The empty humility is that which the poets or philosophers thought of the divinity. For the things they thought are lowly and unworthy of God. For what is so emptily lowly as to think wood and stones gods? Of this empty humility the first son is he who is called outside me, that is, their first sense is outside the truth and outside God. The second is Achiman, that is, brother without counsel, which is to leave God, who made us, and to follow strange gods, whom we made. The third sense of error is Thalamin, which is a precipice or suspension, because the last things of this error tend to the precipice and to the depth of hell. These senses of heathenism, as the sons of Enach of the old error, the law cut off, which even according to the letter preaches the true God, the creator of all. But now Caleb goes up to this city of letters and said: Whosoever shall cut down the city of letters and obtain it, I will give him Axa my daughter to wife, etc. Gothoniel, who took the city of letters, is interpreted the answer of God. And he is called the answer of God to whom God answers, that is, to whom he reveals secrets. He, then, who can take the city of letters of the Old Testament and cut away the letter that killeth is the younger brother of Caleb. This am I, who, the letter of the law being cut away, seek in it the spiritual sense. And I cut away the letter when I am not circumcised according to the flesh, nor eat unleavened bread according to the flesh, nor keep the Pasch with the Jews, or the like, etc. For there is promised to me, if I cut down the city of letters, the daughter of my elder brother. For he was the son of Cenez, which is interpreted contempt. For who was so a contempt as we Gentiles, alienated from the conversation of Israel? For my former brother, whose daughter I receive because I cut down the city of letters, was the son of Jephone, which is interpreted conversion. The law, then, gives to me, the younger brother, its daughter, that is, the understanding of itself; whence: The kingdom of God shall be taken from you and shall be given to a nation yielding the fruits thereof. Yet it must be known that the law, whose person we have now given to Caleb, is one thing, and the letter of the Old Testament, that is, the city of letters, another. Having received his daughter, then, I, his younger brother, lead her from her father's house. And as she was coming with me, sitting on the ass which the disciples of Christ loosed, she says to her father: Give me thy blessing, father. And she received the upper Gonechla and the lower Gonechla, that is, the promise of the life that now is and of that which is to come, a hundredfold in this present world and life everlasting in the world to come.

08_marg130: GREGORY. Axa sits upon an ass when the soul presides over the irrational motions of the flesh. Sighing, she asks of her father a watered land, because the grace of tears is to be sought from the Creator with great groaning. For there are some who have already received [the gift] to speak freely for justice, to protect the oppressed, to give to the needy, to have the ardour of faith, but have not yet the grace of tears. These have a southern and dry land, but still need a watered one, because, placed in good works in which they are great and fervent, they ought, from fear of punishment or love of the heavenly kingdom, to lament also the evils which they committed before. Now there are two principal kinds of compunction, because the soul that thirsts for God is pricked first by fear, afterwards by love. For first it moves itself to tears by fear, because while it recalls its evils it dreads eternal punishments for them. But when the dread has been consumed by long grief, a certain security is born from the presumption of pardon, and the mind is inflamed with the love of heavenly joys; and she who before wept lest she should be led to punishment afterwards begins to weep because she is kept from the kingdom. Her father, then, gives her the upper watered ground when she afflicts herself in tears with the desire of the heavenly kingdom; but she receives the lower watered ground when by weeping she dreads the punishments of hell. Now the lower is given first and the upper watered ground afterwards; but because the compunction of love excels in dignity, it was necessary that the upper watered ground be named first and the lower afterwards.
08_interl229: lest they should root up the wheat also together with it
08_marg131: BUT THE JEBUSITE THAT DWELT, etc. ADAMANTIUS. We understand spiritually that the Jebusites, otherwise the Jebusite, dwelt with the Jews in Jerusalem until the present day, according to the parable of the Gospel which says of the cockle: Suffer both to grow, lest you root up the wheat also together. For so in Jerusalem, that is, in the Church, there are Jebusites, namely those who lead a degenerate life, faithful indeed in name, but perverse in acts, or in action and the conversation of sin. For the Church cannot be purged to clearness while it is on earth. There are in it all the saints, in whom is no stain of sin. But lest the wheat be rooted up with the cockle, there are in it some in whom are sins either doubtful or hidden. For those who are manifestly and evidently criminal are to be expelled from the Church. The children of Juda, then, could not destroy the Jebusites, but dwelt with them in Jerusalem until the present day. Jebusite is interpreted treading underfoot. We ought, then, to have the utmost caution and zeal that no one give or suffer scandal, that no one polluted enter into this congregation of the saints. Yet if we cannot cast out those who tread us underfoot, let us at least cast out those whom we can, whose sins are manifest. For where sin is not evident we can cast no one out of the Church. Now those in the Church who tread underfoot are they of whom it is said: Give not that which is holy to dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest perhaps they trample them, etc. These, then, are the Jebusites, who hear the word of God unworthily, and having heard it neither depart like unbelievers nor remain like the faithful, but, having received the knowledge of the mysteries and searched out the more secret things of our faith, turn and assail us, and break our hearts with contradictions, trampling the pearls of the word of God and staining the ornaments of the faith. These the children of Juda could not cast out of Jerusalem until the present day.
08_marg132: UNTIL THE PRESENT DAY, etc. The same. [It means] the eternity of the age, after the manner of Scripture; but this cannot stand according to the letter. For how does the Jebusite dwell with the children of Juda in Jerusalem as long as this age lasts, when not even the children of Juda dwell there for ever?
08_marg133: [By] treading underfoot, according to the second [sense, are meant] those who make scandal in the Church, and those who, having received the knowledge of the mysteries, trample the pearls of the word of God by assailing them.
08_marg134: Jerusalem is interpreted vision of peace. If, then, Jerusalem, that is, the vision of peace, is built in our heart, and we behold and keep in our heart Christ, who is ever our peace, if indeed we are so fixed and steadfast in this vision of peace that no thought of sin rises into our heart, we can say that we are Jerusalem and that none is with us but the saints alone. But now, even if we come to great perfection and cultivate ourselves with the highest zeal, I think none is so pure as not to be stained by some thought. It is certain, then, that the Jebusites too dwell with the children of Juda in Jerusalem. Yet we must labour daily to cast them out of Jerusalem; but they cannot all be cast out at once.
